scope: Read-only local installed SDK source and project worker, no simulation or new response labels. No proven runtime cause identified.
findings: World.step(render=False) invokes SimulationContext.step→PhysicsContext._step exactly once when playing; PhysicsContext calls native simulate(get_physics_dt(),current_time). Rendering substep ratio is explicitly not used for render=False.

PhysicsContext.set_physics_dt authors integer stepsPerSecond=int(1/dt); for480/960/1920 Hz this matches requested integer Hz. The getter ultimately uses SimulationManager physics-scene dt. Runtime nominal/actual dt must still be recorded.
SimulationContext.current_time accumulates actual physics callback step_size and counts steps separately; current clock checks therefore test actual stepped time, not only a requested loop index.

Experimental RigidPrim.apply_forces defaults local_frame=False and passes native is_global=True with float32 force data. Source reveals no extra dt multiplication or impulse interpretation at the Python wrapper level. Native accumulation/reset semantics remain an engine behavior to isolate experimentally.

SimulationContext.render disables playSimulations during app.update, and manual stepping bypasses app.update. Replicator step(delta_time=0) disables automatic timeline advance; ordinary manual timeline advancement branch tests a truthy nonzero delta. There is no source proof that capture adds a positive dt physics step.

Capture freshness guard checks world clock and display/sensor agreement against q captured before rendering. It does not re-read deformable positions/velocities, rigid poses/velocities, or physics-step count after capture. A hypothetical zero-dt state/constraint update would not be ruled out by clock alone; not observed/proven.

Proposed instrumentation only: compare actual body q/qdot/rigid poses/velocities, current_time_step_index or SimulationManager count, runtime physics dt and scene Hz before/after paused sensor sync; separately test a free rigid body under a known force to isolate force impulse/timestep semantics. Do not alter production worker or tune physical values on current nonconverged labels.
